data.name: Bunyan
data.gender_notes: Bunyan is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A person who travels a long journey, particularly one who encounters many hardships and adventures. The name Bunyan carries the meaning “Traveler” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Bunyan usually hope their child will grow to embody traveler and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes perseverance and determination in one's faith and journey through life.
data.etymology: Bunyan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Traveler.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bunyan total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_arabic.name: بنيان
in_arabic.long_meaning: بنيان هو اسم عربي يعني البناء أو البنية القوية، ويأتي من الجذر العربي ب-ن-ي، ويتعلق ببناء الأشياء والمباني، كما يرمز إلى القوة والتماسك في الإسلام

in_urdu.name: بنیان
in_urdu.long_meaning: بنیان ایک عربی نام ہے جو مضبوط بنیاد یا تعمیر کا معنی رکھتا ہے، جو عربي جڑ ب-ن-ي سے اخذ ہوا ہے، اور اسلام میں قوت اور استحکام کی علامت ہے

in_hindi.name: बुन्यान
in_hindi.long_meaning: बुन्यान एक अरबी नाम है जिसका अर्थ है मजबूत नींव या निर्माण, जो अरबी जड़ ब-न-य से लिया गया है, और इस्लाम में ताकत और स्थिरता का प्रतीक है

in_pashto.name: بنیان
in_pashto.long_meaning: بنیان د عربي نوم دی چې قوي بنياد یا د جوړښت معنی لري، چې د عربي ریښ ب-ن-ي څخه اخیستل شوی دی، او په اسلام کې د قوت او استحکام символ دی

in_english.name: Bunyan
in_english.long_meaning: Bunyan is an Arabic name meaning strong foundation or building, derived from the Arabic root b-n-y, related to construction and strength, symbolizing power and stability in Islamic tradition

data.cultural_impact: The name "Bunyan" is of Arabic origin, meaning "traveler" or " journeyman." In Islamic culture, the concept of the journey or the pilgrimage holds great significance. The Hajj, which is the journey to Mecca, is one of the Five Pillars of Islam. The name "Bunyan" may be viewed as a reflection of the spiritual journey that every Muslim is encouraged to undertake throughout their life. The struggle and adventure of the journey mirrors the challenges and hardships faced in life, and the perseverance and faith required to overcome them.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Islamic tradition, the journey towards spiritual growth and enlightenment is seen as a lifelong process. The name "Bunyan" symbolizes the idea of being on this continual journey of self-discovery and personal transformation. It reflects the belief that life is a spiritual adventure and that each day presents new opportunities for growth and devotion to God. The name can serve as a reminder to seek knowledge, pursue righteous deeds, and seek closeness to Allah at every opportunity.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abd al-Hakam, 'Futūḥ al-Shām' (Conquest of Syria), c. 830 CE The name Bunyan carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Bunyan is mentioned as a Christian Arab chief who surrendered to Caliph al-Ma'mun's forces in Damascus. He was granted safe conduct and became a client (mawla) of the Caliph.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn al-Athir, 'Al-Kāmil fi al-Tārīkh' (The Comprehensive History), 1233 CE The name Bunyan carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Bunyan is mentioned as the commander of the Christian militia of the County of Tripoli in the Levant during the Crusades. He is renowned for his military prowess and is known to have led several successful campaigns against the Crusaders.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Bunyan' is of Islamic origin and holds significant historical and literary importance. It is most famously associated with the story of Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf, a prominent figure during the Umayyad Caliphate in the late 7th century. Bunyan is also the name of the protagonist in 'The Book of Bunyan', a notable work of Arabic literature. Today, Bunyan is a topic of interest for scholars and history enthusiasts on platforms such as Goodreads, Academia.edu, and Amazon Kindle, where they can access scholarly articles, books, and discussions related to Bunyan and the broader context of Islamic history and ancient civilizations.
